The '''2019–20 Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball team''' represented [[Vanderbilt University]] in the [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. They were coached by [[Jerry Stackhouse]] in his first season at Vanderbilt. The Commodores played their home games at [[Memorial Gymnasium (Vanderbilt University)|Memorial Gymnasium]] in [[Nashville, Tennessee]] as members of the [[Southeastern Conference]]. They finished the season 11–21, 3–15 in SEC play to finish in last place. They lost in the first round of the [[2020 SEC men's basketball tournament|SEC tournament]] to [[2019–20 Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball team|Arkansas]].

Following a 90–64 loss to [[2019–20 South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball team|South Carolina]] on January 25, Vanderbilt tied [[Sewanee Tigers|Sewanee]] for the most consecutive conference losses in SEC history, 24, which was set from 1938 to 1940.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/college/vanderbilt/2020/01/25/vanderbilt-basketball-sec-regular-season-losing-streak-south-carolina/4517624002/ |title=Vanderbilt basketball ties 80-year-old record with 24th straight SEC regular-season loss |last=Sparks |first=Adam |publisher=[[The Tennessean]] |date=January 25, 2020 |access-date=January 25, 2020}}</ref>

In the following game at [[2019–20 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]] on January 29, the Commodores broke the SEC record for consecutive conference losses with 25.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401166315 |title=Kentucky hands Vanderbilt record 25th straight SEC loss |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=January 29, 2020 |access-date=January 30, 2020}}</ref>

==Previous season==
They finished the season 9–23, 0–18 in SEC play to finish in 14th place. They are the first SEC team to go winless in a season since the 1953-1954 Georgia Tech team, and the first team ever in the 18 game conference schedule.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/26213289/lsu-fans-deride-ad-sec-title-clinching-rout|title=LSU fans deride AD during SEC title-clinching rout|last=|first=|date=10 March 2019|work=ESPN.com|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190310124911/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/26213289/lsu-fans-deride-ad-sec-title-clinching-rout |archive-date=2019-03-10 |access-date=10 March 2019}}</ref> They followed this winless in conference play season with a loss to Texas A&M in the first round of the SEC tournament, extending their losing streak to 20 games, to finish the season with a combined 0–19 conference record.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/college/vanderbilt/2019/03/13/sec-basketball-tournament-2019-vanderbilt-texas-a-m-billy-kennedy-bryce-drew/3125127002/|title=Vanderbilt's worst basketball season ever ends with SEC Tournament loss to Texas A&M|last=|first=|date=|website=|publisher=The Tennessean|accessdate=13 March 2019}}</ref> As a result of the unprecedented season, third-year head coach [[Bryce Drew]] was fired on March 22, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/college/vanderbilt/2019/03/22/vanderbilt-basketball-bryce-drew-fired/3196259002/|title=Vanderbilt basketball coach Bryce Drew reacts to firing in his first tweet|website=[[The Tennessean]]}}</ref>
